claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr oxidizes rapidly in oxygen-rich environments at high temperature.
Rapid oxidation of untreated HfNbTaTiZr degrades its surface integrity and mechanical properties.
A diffusion-based surface aluminization treatment followed by a short high-temperature anneal can create a continuous Al2O3 layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminization treatment will produce a thin, dense, and adherent alumina scale.
Aluminum introduced by the treatment diffuses to the surface and reacts with ambient oxygen at high temperature to form alumina.
The alumina scale acts as a barrier to further oxygen ingress.
Restricting aluminization to the surface will significantly reduce internal oxidation.
Because the treatment is surface-limited, the bulk microstructure of HfNbTaTiZr will remain largely unaltered.
The bulk microstructure of cast HfNbTaTiZr confers its ductility and yield strength.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will have lower oxidation weight gain than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr during exposure at 1000 °C in air.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will form a thinner oxide layer than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr during exposure at 1000 °C in air.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will retain high-temperature yield strength comparable to untreated cast material.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will retain tensile ductility comparable to untreated cast material.
The proposed effectiveness boundary is exposure at 1000 °C in air for approximately 100 hours and mechanical strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis requires both improved oxidation resistance and retained mechanical performance, but the falsification rule uses a conjunction: it requires inadequate oxidation improvement and excessive mechanical degradation simultaneously. Thus, failure of either required outcome alone would not falsify the hypothesis under the stated rule.
